verdict.rationale: Spline documents a first-party MCP server that lets external agents such as Claude, Cursor and Codex "drive Spline" directly in the open editor tab, which is a write path for agents. However, it only runs bundled in the desktop app, its specific create/modify tools are not documented in the evidence, and there is no REST or file-level write API (the Code API controls exported runtime scenes, not design files). missing for 10: documented MCP tool list showing which create/modify operations are supported, a write-capable REST/headless API that works without an open desktop editor, a plugin surface, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven edits.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create or modify designs programmatically — through a write-capable API, plugin surface, or MCP tools — not just read them

citations.quote: Spline MCP Server — drive Spline from Claude, Cursor, Codex and other MCP clients, straight into your open editor tab.
The **Spline MCP Server** connects AI coding tools like **Claude**, **Cursor**, **Codex**, and **Antigravity** directly to your Spline editor.
The MCP server is bundled in the desktop app, so connecting Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Antigravity or ChatGPT to your editor only works here
There is no REST API, no machine-readable spec, no hosted reference or runner
